headline: Simulations reveal allosteric gating and conformational switching in diverse proteins
label: Protein Conformational Dynamics Simulations
summary: Recent atomistic simulations of transporters, enzymes, and NLRP3 and MLKL signalling proteins resolve allosteric pathways at atomic resolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread is simulation-derived mapping of allosteric and conformational coupling within individual proteins, not a shared target class. Adaptive steered MD of b0,+AT identifies W230 side-chain flipping as a dynamic arginine-transport gate signalled via TM5 and TM6. Markov state modelling of MLKL proteoforms indicates allosteric switching toward the open state, and network analysis of human glutathione synthetase reveals ligand-dependent inter-subunit coupling. Multi-scale simulations place NEK7 effects at distinct stages of the NLRP3 monomer transition. Structural mapping links Leigh syndrome Complex I mutations to protein-glass packing and Marcus electron-transfer bottlenecks, while UCH-L1 knot topology is proposed to suppress LLPS and aggregation. These are computational predictions, and the new element is the attribution of function to specific dynamic or topological features.
